title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Tulsa, OK: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Tulsa exchanger, vessel, skid and pipeline welders: Part C code choice, Part B travel, eligibility. Online or at your shop.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Tulsa: Six Days for Heat Exchanger, Pressure Vessel and Pipeline Welding Inspectors
html:
Tulsa's welding economy grew out of oil and never really left it. The companies that once drilled and refined here now build the equipment the energy industry runs on: air-cooled heat exchangers, pressure vessels, skids, compressor packages, storage tanks and pipeline components shipped across the country and abroad. Add the pipeline companies headquartered downtown, the crude hub at Cushing to the west, a refinery on the Arkansas River and one of the largest airline maintenance bases anywhere, and the result is a metro where inspecting welds is steady, skilled work. Job postings for those inspection roles in Tulsa commonly list the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) as a requirement or a strong preference.

Atlantis NDT has a six-day course that prepares Tulsa-area welders, fitters, shop QC inspectors, NDT technicians and engineers for the CWI examination. The division of roles is simple: AWS writes and grades the exam and grants the certificate, and Atlantis handles preparation and nothing else. It cannot certify anyone, it has never seen the exam's content, and AWS has given the course no approval or endorsement. Whether a candidate qualifies, on education, work history and eyesight, is a matter between that person and AWS. Someone studying alone works online through Atlantis's notes, a study schedule and its own practice sets, and puts questions to an instructor by message. A fabricator can instead host all six days at its plant for a group of its people. A full day-by-day breakdown appears on the AWS CWI exam prep overview.

The heat-exchanger belt of northeast Oklahoma

Northeast Oklahoma has become a center for air-cooled heat exchanger manufacturing, the large fin-fan coolers that sit beside compressor stations, gas plants and refineries. AXH air-coolers runs a large manufacturing complex in Claremore and has announced a second campus in Sapulpa. In Skiatook, just north of Tulsa, Worldwide Exchangers has built air-cooled units since the mid-1990s and also makes shell-and-tube exchangers; the company has been part of SHECO since 2016. Smaller fabricators across Tulsa, Rogers and Creek counties supply headers, structures and related equipment.

An air-cooled exchanger is a welding inspector's education in one product. The headers are pressure parts, usually designed to ASME Section VIII, Division 1, and built to the API 661 standard for air-cooled exchangers in petroleum and gas service. Header boxes involve thick plate, full-penetration corner and groove welds, and plug or cover plate construction where access for repair is limited. Nozzles and their reinforcement need careful fit-up. The steel structure, fan decks and walkways are welded to AWS D1.1. Tube-to-tubesheet joints may be expanded, welded or both, depending on the specification.

Shops building code pressure parts work under an ASME certificate with an Authorized Inspector reviewing their work, and their own QC staff do the day-to-day checking before the AI arrives. That in-house role is where many Tulsa CWIs work: checking material traceability, verifying that each welder is qualified for the joint, watching preheat on thick headers, measuring weld size and reinforcement, and keeping the paperwork the code requires. Atlantis supports this sector with pressure vessel inspection in Tulsa and weld inspection services at customer facilities.

Pipeline country: headquarters downtown, tank farms at Cushing

Several major midstream companies, including Williams and ONEOK, are headquartered in Tulsa, and the engineering, construction management and integrity work behind their pipeline networks supports a large local workforce. West of the city, Cushing is one of the most important crude oil storage and trading hubs in North America, ringed by tank farms and pipeline connections.

That activity creates three kinds of welding inspection work. On the right-of-way, construction and repair welds follow API 1104, which the federal gas and hazardous liquid pipeline regulations incorporate by reference. Station piping, meter skids and pump and compressor packages are built in local fabrication shops to ASME B31.3 or B31.8 with ASME Section IX qualifications. Storage tanks at Cushing and elsewhere are erected to API 650, with welded shell, bottom and roof seams that need visual inspection as construction proceeds. Atlantis works with pipeline owners through pipeline NDT consulting in Tulsa.

Refining, aviation maintenance and the inland port

Tulsa still has a refinery along the Arkansas River on the city's west side, and its maintenance and turnaround programs follow the same ASME and API documents as plants on the Gulf Coast. Atlantis covers refinery owners through refining NDT consulting for Tulsa.

At Tulsa International Airport, American Airlines operates a major maintenance and engineering base. Airframe structure is mostly fastened, but ground support equipment, tooling, fixtures and some engine and component work involve welding, often to AWS D17.1 or a manufacturer specification. Inspectors in that environment work with small parts, thin material and strict documentation.

Northeast of the city, the Tulsa Port of Catoosa sits at the head of the McClellan-Kerr Arkansas River Navigation System. Its barge access lets local fabricators ship oversized vessels, exchanger bundles and modules that are too big for highways, which is one reason heavy fabrication clusters around it. Building and bridge projects across Oklahoma add structural work under codes adopted by the state from the International Building Code and under the Oklahoma Department of Transportation's bridge specifications.

Who hires welding inspectors in the Tulsa area

Exchanger and pressure vessel manufacturers are the largest group. They want QC inspectors who understand ASME Section VIII and Section IX, can read a weld map, and can keep pace with production without missing a hold point.

Skid and package fabricators building compressor, meter and process skids for midstream customers need inspectors comfortable with B31.3 piping, structural bases welded to D1.1, and customer specifications that change from order to order.

Pipeline construction and integrity contractors put CWIs on right-of-way spreads and repair digs, where API 1104 and the operator's procedures govern. Tank builders erecting new storage at Cushing and other terminals need inspectors for API 650 construction.

Refinery maintenance contractors, structural fabricators, and testing and inspection agencies round out the list. Aviation maintenance employers hire some CWIs, mostly for ground equipment and tooling. Inspection companies that pair visual weld inspection with ultrasonic, magnetic particle and penetrant testing value candidates who can do both, which is why many Tulsa CWIs also pursue NDT certification through their employer.

The Tulsa Section of AWS

AWS local sections are grouped into districts. Tulsa has its own section in District 17, the same district as the Oklahoma City Section. Meetings and tours put candidates in a room with exchanger shop QC managers, pipeline welding engineers, inspectors and welding instructors, many of whom have taken the CWI exam. Their advice on code book choice and on preparing for the practical is often worth more than a week of solitary study. For current officers and meeting locations, use the District 17 listing on aws.org.

Learning to weld in Tulsa

Tulsa has unusually deep welding education for a city of its size. Tulsa Tech, the area's career and technology center, runs a full-time Welding Fabricator program. Tulsa Welding School, a private trade school that has trained welders in the city for decades, also operates here. Union apprenticeships and in-house training at the large fabricators add more routes into the trade.

Graduates leave these programs with hand skills and code awareness, but AWS will not accept them for the CWI exam until they have built up welding-related work experience. For most, the CWI is a target several years into a career, often after time as a shop welder or a QC helper. Starting a log of jobs, codes and supervisors from day one makes the eventual application far easier.

Part C code books for people who build pressure equipment

Each candidate brings one book into the open-book code test. AWS's current menu names a specific edition for each choice, including the structural steel code AWS D1.1, the pipeline standard API 1104, the bridge code D1.5, aluminum, railroad and aerospace codes, an ISO option, and an ASME choice combining the Section IX qualification rules with power and process piping. Confirm editions on aws.org before buying.

For Tulsa, the decision usually follows the product:

  • Exchanger, vessel and skid shops: the ASME choice, because Section IX qualification is the daily language of code pressure work. Note that Section VIII itself is not part of that option, so construction rules for vessels are learned on the job.
  • Structural steel, exchanger structures, tank and port steel: AWS D1.1, a good general base that also leads naturally to other endorsements.
  • Pipeline construction and integrity work: API 1104.
  • Aviation ground equipment and component work: AWS D17.1, if your employer works to it.

Helpful reading before Day 4: the overview of Section IX qualification, the pipeline welding standard summary and the structural code overview. For how procedures and welder tests fit together, see the WPS, PQR and WPQ article. Atlantis neither writes nor qualifies welding procedures, but the exam assumes you can verify work against one.

Sitting the exam from Tulsa

Two of the three parts, the 150-question Fundamentals paper and the open-book code test of roughly 50 to 65 items, are delivered on screen at Prometric test centers. AWS cites more than 100 such centers in the United States. You book them using the eligibility code printed in your AWS confirmation letter.

Part B (Practical) puts AWS's own gauges and test pieces in your hands, pairs those tasks with 46 written questions, and happens only at a seminar site on a date AWS fixes. Tulsa candidates may need to travel, so confirm the closest Part B site and its dates on aws.org before choosing a study timeline. The pass mark is 72% on every part.

AWS sets its own exam and seminar charges and lists them on aws.org. To estimate books, travel to the practical and time away from the shop, try the CWI exam spending calculator, and read how results vary by exam part to see where to focus.

The six days, with exchanger shop examples

  1. Fundamentals I. Welding processes, joint types and groove geometry, AWS A3.0 terminology and AWS A2.4 symbols. Exchanger shops supply plenty of header drawings full of groove and fillet symbols to practise on.
  2. Fundamentals II. How carbon and alloy steels react to welding heat, what mechanical tests reveal, why discontinuities form, the reach and limits of each NDT method, safe practice and the ethical duties of an inspector. Thick-plate preheat and hydrogen control get extra attention for header work.
  3. Practical. Gauge reading, weld size and contour, misalignment, and acceptance decisions against a supplied document set. Plant-based groups practise on their own production welds with gauges from their own QC lockers; Atlantis does not send replica kits.
  4. Code application. Learning the layout of the chosen book so that variables, tables and acceptance limits can be found in moments rather than minutes.
  5. Timed practice. Full-length practice papers for each part under time pressure, followed by a careful review of every miss.
  6. Final review. Re-teaching weak topics, planning exam-day pacing, and checking the AWS application package.

Atlantis writes all of its practice material from the AWS topic outline; nothing in it comes from a real AWS exam. The course explains what will be covered and makes no promise about the result.

Experience rules for shop welders and field hands

AWS links the years of welding-related work you need to your level of schooling, and the full scale is on the course overview. In Tulsa terms: a welder who stopped at a high school diploma or equivalent needs five years; a Tulsa Tech or Tulsa Welding School graduate would normally be in the trade-course row, which asks for four; a two-year degree in engineering, engineering technology or a physical science asks for two. AWS makes the final call on which row applies.

Shop welders usually have tidy employment records. Field hands on pipeline spreads or tank jobs may have worked for many contractors in short stints, so keep a running record with the employer, location, dates, processes, codes and a supervisor who can vouch for each job. Eyesight is a separate requirement, tested on an AWS-specified form within a period AWS sets before the exam.

After the CWI: endorsements, NDT and next steps

A CWI runs on the nine-year AWS cycle, with interim renewals and a recertification decision at the end. Tulsa inspectors often add an API 1104 endorsement or the magnetic particle and penetrant testing endorsements, and some later aim for the Senior CWI credential.

Many move into NDT as well. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, certification to perform NDT comes from the employer under its written practice; Atlantis delivers training to that standard, from VT Level 1 upward, with local details under NDT training in Tulsa and employer options under corporate NDT training in Tulsa. You can also rehearse weld inspection in the Practical NDT welding workshop.

Candidates across the region can compare CWI exam prep in Kansas City, Dallas and Baton Rouge.

Request a Tulsa quote

Let Atlantis know the number of candidates, the code book each will bring to Part C, and whether they will study online or together at your shop, including its address. The Tulsa quote form takes those details, and Atlantis answers within one business day.

faq.q: Which Part C code book suits an air-cooled exchanger shop?
faq.a: Most exchanger and vessel shop candidates choose the ASME option because Section IX qualification governs their daily work. Section VIII is not part of that option, so vessel construction rules are learned on the job.

faq.q: Is a CWI useful if I work on pipelines out of Tulsa?
faq.a: Yes. Spread contractors and repair crews often want a CWI on site, and API 1104, the standard federal pipeline rules point to, is on the AWS list of Part C books.

faq.q: Where do Tulsa candidates take the exam?
faq.a: Fundamentals and Code Application are on-screen tests you schedule with Prometric after AWS issues your eligibility code. Part B runs only at AWS seminar sites on fixed dates, so you may need to travel; confirm the nearest one on aws.org.

faq.q: Does Atlantis teach the course in Tulsa?
faq.a: Not in a classroom. Individuals study online with an instructor for questions, and a Tulsa employer can host the six days at its own shop for a group. Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad.
AWS writes and grades the exam and grants the certification. Atlantis does the preparation work, never has access to the questions, and has received no AWS endorsement or approval.

faq.q: I graduated from a Tulsa welding school. How soon can I sit the exam?
faq.a: Not straight away. AWS requires welding-related work experience on top of education, and completed trade courses usually mean four years of experience. AWS decides how your training is classified.

faq.q: Can on-site training use our own production welds?
faq.a: Yes. When the six days run at your facility, the practical exercises can use your own gauges and production weld samples. Atlantis does not supply replica kits.

faq.q: Are the practice questions from real exams?
faq.a: No. Every question is written by Atlantis from the topics AWS publishes, and none comes from an actual AWS examination.

faq.q: Can I add NDT certification later?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis trains technicians to ASNT SNT-TC-1A, after which the company you work for issues the certification through its written practice. Details are on NDT training in Tulsa.

faq.q: How do I get a quote?
faq.a: Use the Tulsa quote request with headcount, code books and your shop address. Atlantis replies within one business day.
